page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced 1:4 resource ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic instructions. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n2d-standard-8 delivers strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and Geekbench scores fall consistently within the average range. The instance demonstrates average throughput for static web serving, Redis SET operations, and database operations. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is relatively weak, landing in the bottom 25%, which highlights a potential bottleneck for highly parallelized compression tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC hardware profile offers a stable and predictable resource density suitable for standard enterprise workloads without the premium of specialized memory or compute-optimized tiers. The balanced configuration makes it well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, software compilation, database operations, and light language model inference tasks.
